revision_summary:
Primary fix needed: resolve and flag the speaker/rep-name attribution ambiguity. The transcript opens with speaker_0 saying 'This is Parker' at 00:02, but the entire qualifying conversation (credit qualifier, ownership qualifier, booking) is conducted by speaker_2, while speaker_1 is the customer. Stage 3 sets rep_name to 'Parker' without acknowledging this three-speaker inconsistency, and builds its intro_legitimacy_omission cherry-pick moment starting at 00:10 while never surfacing the actual 00:02 opening line. Add a flag noting the speaker-label ambiguity in this transcript and clarify (or hedge) the rep_name attribution accordingly — this affects confidence in every rep-attributed quote in the brief.

Secondary fix: correct the script_coverage 'prior_design' quote attribution — the quote 'Did you get solar with us, or was it with a different company?' is spoken by the rep at approximately 00:41, not 00:47 (00:47 is the customer's reply beginning 'It was Freedom at the time'). Fix the timestamp.

Tertiary fix: soften the definitive claim that 'the company name (Ion) is never said aloud on this call' — given ASR garbling throughout (note the duplicated-text artifacts elsewhere in the transcript, e.g. 02:19), this should be framed as 'not detected in this transcript, possible ASR gap' rather than stated as fact in a coaching note.

Minor addition: credit the rep's clean scope-deferral at 01:31 ('one of our specialists... go over the battery options... answer any questions') as a positive setter_scope_discipline example in cherry_pick_moments, rather than only raising scope-restraint as a rejected alternative_hypothesis inside the curiosity_creation_failure entry.

Also reconsider applying orphaned_flow and intros.standard as cleanly as Stage 3 does — both are being stretched to a scenario (inbound callback + battery-only retrofit on existing system) that sits at the edge of what those schema sections were designed for. Flag as a schema-coverage gap rather than treating the schema's fit as given.
